questions: On the slalom, do line_loss_events fall below 1.0, and does max_error drop below 0.06 m? Report completion_time for any finish.
Does s-bend steering_oscillation rise above 0.35 with the longer lead, or does s-bend finish count fall below 17/20?
Does the oval still finish 20/20 at about 1.85 s?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If slalom line loss is unchanged at about 1.0 with max_error at or above 0.06, report max_error at exit and the heading at the first line loss so the next step can target the controller's entry speed or the sensor geometry. If s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.35, return the lead to 0.06 m.

intent: Keep the iteration 5 design (±0.036 m span at 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body and mass unchanged). Change only the sensor lead from y=0.06 to y=0.07 m, the one untested geometry variable. The Integrator should keep the weights, kp and kd unchanged so the race isolates the lead. Expected: slalom line loss falls below 1.0 and max_error drops toward 0.06, with the first slalom finishes possible, while the oval holds 20/20 and the s-bend holds at or above 17/20.
learning: Five variants have now failed the slalom at max_error 0.062 to 0.064, so no single span, footprint, lead or track value has cleared it. Lead 0.04 m was clearly worse, and the 0.07 m lead tests whether a longer look-ahead helps. If that also fails, the limit is likely the robot's yaw response (mass and body_length set yaw inertia), which I would test next.
rationale: Iteration 5 (±0.036 m span, 12 mm footprints, 0.06 m lead, wheel_track 0.10 m) is the best so far at 653.3. The oval finished 20/20 at 1.85 s, and the s-bend finished 18/20 with steering_oscillation 0.335, under the 0.35 jitter limit. The slalom is still 0/20, with 1.0 line-loss events and max_error 0.0644, past the 0.06 m limit. Its line loss is unchanged at 1.0, so reach is not the limit either. Across five variants, the slalom has failed at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 whatever the span, footprint, lead or track. Lead 0.04 m was clearly worse on every track, but a longer lead of 0.07 m has not been tested. The prior rule says that if slalom line loss stays at about 1.0 and max_error stays at 0.06 or more, the lead is the next variable. The longer lead lets the controller see the line earlier, which may cover the slalom's direction changes. I keep the best-scoring span (±0.036 m, 0.012 m pitch) and change only sensor y from 0.06 to 0.07 m, so the result isolates lead. Signal scale is unchanged because the weights and span are unchanged. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 or max_error drops below 0.06, with a first slalom finish possible. The risk is more s-bend phase lag and jitter, so steering_oscillation on all tracks must be reported.
